To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the terms calibration and validation are not interchangeable, that model calibration is a process, that model validation is a process, and that model calibration and validation are two different processes.

(1) the term calibration refers to the process of adjusting model parameters to minimize the difference between the model output and measured data, while the term validation refers to the process that is performed to determine the ability of the model to simulate a particular system or process; (2) the term validation should not be used to describe the process of determining whether or not the model is appropriate for the system under study; (3) the term verification should not be used as a synonym for calibration or validation; (
the terms “calibration” and “validation” should be used to refer to model evaluation activities that occur prior to and after model application, respectively.

providing a consistent terminology for writing about hydrology, water quality, and modeling, and in particular for writing about modeling calibration and validation.
